title: Trace pairing and microbench incident playbook
content:
Purpose
---
This playbook describes a lightweight, repeatable approach for pairing production traces with focused microbench experiments to root-cause performance regressions that manifest as latency spikes, KV cache staleness, or kernel scheduling anomalies. It is meant for on-call and eng teams triaging intermittent regressions that are NOT trivially reproducible locally.

Motivation / Background
---
We frequently see regressions that only show up in production trace samples: a spike in 95th/99th latency, sudden increase in kernel-context switches, or an apparent KV cache miss storm. Full-system replays are expensive and brittle. Trace pairing is a middle path: extract minimal trace slices (request+dependencies), synthesize matching microbench workloads, and run parameterized microbench experiments to observe the same behaviors under controlled kernel/kv/host permutations.

When to use this playbook
---
- Incident shows a cluster of related traces with unusual kernel timings or high per-token latency variance.
- Previous attempts (replay or e2e bench) failed to reproduce.
- You have at least one production trace that includes scheduler, kernel, and kv-cache span metadata.

Quick triage (5–15m)
---
1) Gather evidence
   - Pull representative traces (trace IDs) from observability: trace IDs, route, model, model_version, sequence_length, kv-hit-rate metadata.
   - Note impacted hosts/regions and time window.
2) Classify symptom
   - Latency distribution shift? (p95/p99 up)
   - KV miss ratio spike? (prefix misses, kvcache evictions)
   - Kernel scheduling tail? (context switch bursts, long syscalls)
3) Attach severity and owner
   - If user-visible and sustained: page oncall and file INF ticket.
   - Assign a primary investigator (PI).

Trace-pairing procedure (detailed)
---
Goal: produce a microbench run that "matches" the production trace in the minimal set of observables (token inter-arrival, kv hit/miss patterns, kernel wake/sleep patterns).

A) Trace extraction
  - Use trace-exporter to pull raw spans and annotations for the timeframe.
  - Export artifacts: request payload (prompt), model_id, model_version, kv-keys referenced (if listed), sequence-length distribution, and per-token latencies if available.
  - Save into benchlab/trace-pairs/<incident-id>/trace-<traceid>.json (artifact naming convention).

B) Synthesize request workload
  - From trace JSON, derive a minimal request script that reproduces the prompt(s) and streaming cadence.
  - If streaming partials in production, mimic token inter-arrival times: microbench supports a --token-delay-ms parameter. Start with median and 99th percentiles from trace.

C) KV cache alignment
  - Key step: reproduce kv-cache state (warm/cold) exactly or parameterize it.
  - Modes:
    * cold: clear kvcache before run (--kv-clear)
    * warm-prefill: use benchlab prefill utility to insert keys seen in trace (--kv-prefill-file)
    * churn: generate background eviction noise to approximate contention (--kv-churn-rate)
  - Capture kvcache metrics in production (prefill ratio, evictions/sec) to pick prefill/churn parameters.

D) Kernel scheduling knobs
  - Run microbench with alternative kernel configs available in lab:
    * default scheduler (baseline)
    * isolated-cpus + irq affinity (noisy-neighbour mitigation)
    * cgroups v2 throttling scenario
  - Add noise drivers to emulate CPU frequency scaling or host load (--cpu-burn/--syscall-burst).

E) Iterative runs and metrics to compare
  - For each experiment, capture the following artifacts: microtrace (continuous span timeline), per-token latencies, kv-hit-rate telemetry, perf counters (context-switches, migrations), and kernel symbol samples (if enabled).
  - Compare with production trace using a lightweight similarity heuristic: token-latency-shape (DTW or CDF L1), kv-hit delta, and context-switch difference. Record score in benchlab/trace-pairs/<incident-id>/scores.csv.

Checklist / Runbook (step-by-step)
---
1) Create incident dir: benchlab/trace-pairs/<YYYYMMDD>-<incident-id>/
2) Save production artifacts: trace JSONs, route config snapshot, model binary tag, host profile.
3) Baseline local run: microbench --trace-input trace.json --run-id baseline --collect-all
4) If baseline reproduces, capture diff and file INF ticket with minimal repro. Otherwise continue.
5) KV experiments: run cold, prefill, and churn scenarios. Label runs accordingly.
6) Kernel experiments: isolated-cpu, added host load, and scheduler variant runs.
7) For each run, attach logs, perf.data, microtrace, and bench run metadata to the incident dir and the INF ticket.
8) Summarize findings as hypothesis statements (see template) and recommended mitigations.

Hypothesis template (use in ticket/PR body)
---
- Symptom: concise description (e.g., "p99 token latency increased by 60ms for route /v1/generate between 2025-01-10T02:14-02:22 UTC").
- Evidence: trace IDs, microbench run IDs, score differences, perf counters.
- Root-cause hypothesis: (one-sentence).
- Experiments run: list run-IDs and brief outcome.
- Recommended mitigation(s): short-term and long-term.

Severity & action matrix (quick)
---
- Sev1: sustained production regression across many customers >30m -> hotfix + rollback + postmortem.
- Sev2: intermittent with clear triage path -> immediate investigation, scheduler/kv config toggles as mitigations.
- Sev3: single-customer or non-critical -> investigate next-day with benchlab experiments.

Artifacts and naming conventions (important)
---
- benchlab/trace-pairs/<incident>/trace-<traceid>.json  (extracted production trace)
- benchlab/trace-pairs/<incident>/microrun-<mode>-<id>.tar.gz  (microbench artifacts: perf, logs, microtrace)
- benchlab/trace-pairs/<incident>/scores.csv  (run similarity scores)
- benchlab/trace-pairs/<incident>/notes.md  (investigator notes and decisions)

Commands & quick examples
---
- Extract trace: ./tools/trace-exporter pull --trace-id <id> --out benchlab/trace-pairs/INC123/trace-<id>.json
- Run baseline microbench: ./benchlab/microbench --replay-trace benchlab/trace-pairs/INC123/trace-<id>.json --run-id baseline --collect-perf --token-delay-ms-from-trace
- Prefill KV: ./benchlab/kv-prefill --file benchlab/trace-pairs/INC123/kv-keys.txt --target benchlab-lab:11211
- Run churn: ./benchlab/microbench --replay-trace ... --kv-churn-rate 50 --run-id churn-50

Example investigation timeline (toy)
---
- 02:15 - Alert: p99 jump on /v1/chat route.
- 02:21 - Oncall pulls three traces (T1,T2,T3).
- 02:35 - Baseline microbench run does NOT reproduce.
- 03:05 - Prefill run reproduces a smaller but similar latency tail.
- 04:40 - Kernel isolation test reproduces >90% of production tail (run id kernel-iso-001).
- 06:12 - Hypothesis: scheduler preemption combined with cold KV misses amplifies tail. Short-term mitigation: enable cpusets for the route and prefilling on peak nodes.

Investigator notes / heuristics (opinions)
---
- If you can reproduce with a warm prefill but not cold, treat it as kvcache contiguity issue (eviction pattern).
- If context-switches increase without equivalent kv-hit change, suspect background host noise or driver-level syscalls.
- Always check for recent kernel/driver updates on impacted hosts (apt/dkms records).

Unresolved questions / TODOs
---
- How to safely reproduce cross-host network jitter without full cluster replay? (idea: synthetic network delay shim in benchlab).
- Add DTW-based automated similarity scoring to benchlab (ticket INF-4899).
- Standardize microtrace format for easier diffing with production traces.

Appendix A: quick templates
---
- Title: "Incident INC123: trace-pairing summary"
- Hypothesis short: "Scheduler preemption + kvcache prefill mismatch -> amplified p99 latency"
- Suggested PR title: "benchlab: add kernel-iso-config and kv-prefill scenario for INC123"

Notes to self (informal)
---
- Keep experiments small and parameterized. The cheaper we can run a matrix of kv x kernel x token-delay, the faster we get to hypothesis.
- When in doubt, prefill first (warming) — many customer regressions are due to warmed-state interactions.
- Put run metadata (git sha, benchlab image tag) with every artifact.

References
---
- benchlab repo: github.com/redwood-inference/benchlab
- recent incident INF-4721 notes (internal)
- kv-profiles and prefill tooling: benchlab/kv-prefill docs (internal)

--end of playbook--
